Highlights of our win included 12 winners. Simon Maynard and Abi Ekoku won on their BAL debuts. John Regis and Marcus Adam in his debut put the frighteners on Linford Christie.

Admittedly a few of our 'A' team men were on view, with John Barry scoring an easy 1500 win and Abi Ekoku giving us maximum points in the Shot and Discus, but we had no 'B' competitor in two events and the selected 'B' 1500m runner didn't turn up so we were still giving away points unnecessarily.

International honours again fell to John Gladwin and Ernie Obeng while Abi Ekoku becomes a new name for the club honours Board with an England Under 23 appearance, as does Felix Sandy who ran in the World Championships for Sierra Leone.

Other good performances came from Stu' Paton, Paul Cuff, John Wright, Abi Ekoku, Phil Lovell and Peter (I just made it) Farrell. Ian Bland and Derek Capper made their BAL debuts and it was good to see Alistair Johnson, Greggy, Vince and Derek Brown back in the team.

Throws Abi Ekoku made good progress this year. In the Shot he placed 8th in the 'UKs' and 6th at the Pearl Invitation meet at Gateshead before breaking through the 16 metre line for a fine new club record at a Southern Counties match in August.

His choice of Belgrave was as a result of meeting fellow Civil Service athletes Abi Ekoku, Jay Busk and Derrick Williams. He aims to train at Battersea Park with Bob Bridges squad at least once per month.
Individual wins were recorded by Marcus Adam in the sprints, Femi Abejide the Triple Jump, Marcello Bizio the Steeplechase and Jimmy Summers and Abi Ekoku mopping up the Throws.

Many of the pole vaulters failed to qualify and among several of the elite who missed the cut was Mike Edwards who only managed a disappointing 5.10. Abi Ekoku also turned in a below par performance with injury reducing his best discuss throw to 53.80.

As we enter the '91 T & F Season Lenny Paul takes up a new post as 'A' team Captain. The Sectional Captain's jobs remain and are :- Sprints - John Regis, Throws - Abi Ekoku, Jumps - Derek Browne, Distance - Stuart Paton.

The unlucky ones included Abi Ekoku whose start to the season was delayed by injury. He was pipped by Darrin Morris whose selection resulted from his splendid BAL Division 1 debut in claret and gold.

But Jon Ridgeon from Abi Ekoku with first leg man Derek Browne all ran beautifully to do the business, gaining second spot in 41.41. Duane Hart, Darryl Maynard, Rob Turner and Jon Ridgeon just had to run at their very best for us to win and this they did with an exceptionally fine 3:14.4.
